text:
**Short answer:** For most camping trips, get a light unit in the 250–500 Wh range. The Jackery Explorer 300 Plus is the best all-around pick. If you need more power for longer off-grid stays, step up to a 1,000+ Wh model.

## Best by trip type

**Weekend camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)**
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus**: 288 Wh, 300 W AC, about 8.3 lb, around $249. PowerStationGearLab names it best overall for camping and notes a CPAP can run for multiple nights. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) Its editor's note says Jackery's US site no longer lists this model; it has been replaced by the Explorer 300 v2, which has a shorter warranty. Check which version you're buying.
  - Buy: [search Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+300+Plus)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus**: 286 Wh, 600 W AC, about 9.9 lb, around $269–299. It has double the Jackery's AC output for a similar price, so it's the value pick if you run heavier gear. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
  - Buy: [search Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=EcoFlow+River+3+Plus)
- **Bluetti EB3A**: 268 Wh, 600 W AC, around $179. The cheapest real LiFePO4 option in the same class. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
  - Buy: [search Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Bluetti+EB3A)

**Longer trips or running a fridge**
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: 2,042 Wh capacity, about 1,710 Wh usable, 39 lb. OutdoorGearLab's top pick for multi-day off-grid camping, and it can be recharged with solar. It's listed at under $900 on Amazon. It won't run an electric burner or space heater for long. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
  - Buy: [search Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+2000+v2)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: 890 Wh measured, 25.2 lb, 1,800 W AC, about $530 on sale. OutdoorGearLab's best value for most people. It has a noisy fan. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
  - Buy: [search Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Anker+SOLIX+C1000+Gen+2)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**: 1,536 Wh, about 40 lb, IP65 rated for rain and dust, with a comfortable handle. WIRED picks it as best for camping at about $1,079 on Amazon. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)
  - Buy: [search Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+1500+Ultra)

**A deal worth checking: BLUETTI AC180**
A Dealectric page lists the BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W AC, about 16 kg) at $499 with code AFF5OFF, which the page says was tested on 2026-10-21. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180) Dealectric earns a commission on purchases through this link, and I couldn't verify the price or code independently. The store's checkout is the final word. It's a solid mid-size option if you want more capacity than the 300 Wh class.
- Buy: [Dealectric link to BLUETTI's US store](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)

## Quick guidance
- **Pack weight matters.** For tent camping, anything over about 25 lb becomes a chore.
- **CPAP users:** turn the humidifier off. It can roughly triple the draw. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Prices change.** The figures above come from search snippets and may be out of date. Confirm the current price, capacity, and version before buying.
- **Solar:** most of these pair with portable panels, which helps on trips longer than a few days.
